original_question: Can one construct a Khovanov complex for arbitrary virtual knot diagrams, further develop the orientable-atom-based Khovanov homology for large classes of virtual links, and resolve the associated structural questions about K-full and Kho-full knots, optimal diagrams, minimality of classical crossings in virtual diagrams of classical knots, diagram moves preserving optimality, and the possibility of torsion in the B-state of virtual Khovanov homology?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 13, "Khovanov homology," together with its immediate setup in Section 6, "Khovanov and other invariants," and the atom/orientability background in Section 3.1, "Atoms." ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual multi-part open problem: it includes the search for a Khovanov complex for arbitrary virtual diagrams, the existing orientable-atom-based integral theory for large classes of virtual links, and the follow-up questions on K-full/Kho-full knots, optimal diagrams, minimality in classical crossings, optimality-preserving moves, the classical-knot crossing-number comparison, and possible torsion in the B-state. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))
missing_details: The paper makes the coefficient ring explicit: the sought full extension is a Khovanov homology for all virtual knots over the ring of integers, while a Khovanov polynomial over Z_2 for virtuals had already been proposed. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

The paper’s nearest precise description of the existing integral theory is that Khovanov homology with arbitrary coefficient ring can be defined for any link diagram whose corresponding atom is orientable; the phrase "large classes of virtual links" in Problem 13 points back to this orientable-atom condition. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

K-full is not just an informal adjective: the paper defines a K-full virtual knot as one for which there exists a diagram whose leading term, lowest term, or both come from the B-state. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))
Kho-full is defined analogously, but specifically relative to the Khovanov invariant. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

"Optimal diagrams" are the diagrams realizing the K-full or Kho-full property; that definition is needed to interpret the minimality and move-classification questions. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

The minimality question is specifically about the number of classical crossings, not total crossings and not virtual crossings. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

The classical-knot crossing-number question is quantified exactly as follows: if a classical knot K has a minimal classical diagram with n crossings, must every virtual diagram of K have at least n classical crossings? ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

The torsion question is specifically about torsion in the B-state of the virtual Khovanov homology, interpreted as the genuine leading term of some diagram, and the paper says this question uses the formulation of Khovanov homology from references [91] and [78]. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

To make the question fully stand-alone, one should also unpack the paper’s implicit bracket terminology: the B-state is standard all-B smoothing language coming from the bracket-state model introduced earlier in the paper. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

The paper adds one further nearby remark omitted from your draft: analogous questions can also be asked for new Khovanov-type homology theories related to other quantum invariants. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))
refined_question: Can one construct, over the ring of integers, a generalization of the Khovanov complex for virtual knots that works for arbitrary virtual diagrams and extends the existing integral theory for the large class of virtual link diagrams with orientable atom; and, in the formulation of virtual Khovanov homology used in [91] and [78], classify K-full and Kho-full virtual knots, where K-full means that some diagram has its leading term, lowest term, or both coming from the B-state, Kho-full is the analogous notion for the Khovanov invariant, and such diagrams are called optimal; determine whether optimal diagrams are always minimal with respect to the number of classical crossings, classify the diagram moves that preserve optimality, decide whether a classical knot with minimal classical diagram of n crossings can admit any virtual diagram with fewer than n classical crossings, and determine whether any virtual knot can have torsion in the B-state of its Khovanov homology, i.e. in the genuine leading term of some diagram? ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of the paper’s Problem 13 and not of a broader neighboring issue. Section 6 states the motivating open problem—whether a Khovanov-type construction can be generalized to virtual knots in general—while Section 3.1 supplies the crucial orientable-atom condition, and Section 7, Problem 13 collects exactly the extension problem plus the K-full/Kho-full, optimality, minimality, and torsion subquestions. Because the paper itself phrases these as one bundled research agenda rather than as separate equivalent formulations, the sharpest faithful rewrite is a single multi-clause question that keeps all of those parts together and makes the definitions explicit. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))
